title: Prepare a secondary against the engine's exact options
description: While another player resolves a strategy card, a follower can prepare the secondary. The stand-in questions used to be worked out in the browser (the Technology list from the seat's own technologies, Construction sites from the planets it controls, no build list at all for Warfare). The server now answers a read-only question, 'what would my pending secondary ask if it opened now', from the engine's own flow, so the panel shows the real Technology list (including what a planet skip opens) with the way the 4 resources would be paid, the real structure sites, and for Warfare the real production builder on the home system's build list. The answer is as of now: it is refreshed while the panel is open, and the plan is checked against the real question when it opens. The before shots are taken on the commit without the preview and committed; the after shots are regenerated by npm run screenshots -- AS. Synthetic fixtures through a mocked server, not captured engine states.

shots.heading: Before: Technology list estimated in the browser
shots.caption: The list is worked out from the seat's own technologies and says so (Approximate until the real question opens). Technologies that need a planet skip or a waiver are not on it, so they cannot be picked even with a skip toggled. The preparing banner also lay over the top of the modal and covered the skip toggles.

shots.heading: After: the engine's own Technology list
shots.caption: The real research list as the engine would offer it now. With a planet's tech skip toggled a second-row technology is selectable. The banner says the options are exact as of now and re-checked when your turn comes, and shows how the engine would pay the 4 resources.

shots.heading: Before: Warfare could only be followed
shots.caption: The build list is the home system's PRODUCTION, known only to the engine, so following Warfare was the whole plan: the chip reads Follow Warfare and nothing about what to build.

shots.heading: After: the real production builder
shots.caption: Following opens the real production builder on the engine's build list: units, costs, production capacity, fleet supply and the resource budget. Two builds are staged; Save these builds records them by unit, sends nothing and spends nothing. The first build's payment is prepared next in the real payment drawer when the engine would ask for one. The dialog now starts below the preparing banner.

shots.heading: Before: the builder opens empty
shots.caption: When the real production question opens the plan had nothing to say about it, so the builder starts empty and the player stages everything again.

shots.heading: After: the prepared builds are staged
shots.caption: The real builder opens with the prepared builds already staged and the bar says what Confirm does. One click sends them through the builder's own path (one production batch, or its build queue for several); Auto sends the same after its visible delay, and Needs review says why when the builds no longer fit the capacity or the resources.

shots.heading: Variant: the engine would not ask you as of now
shots.caption: If the seat cannot pay the 4 resources right now the window would not open, and the banner says so. Preparing is still allowed: the plan applies if that changes before the turn, and is dropped if the window never opens.

shots.heading: Variant: an older server
shots.caption: A server without the preview message answers with an unknown-message error, which is swallowed (the player sees nothing) and remembered. The panel keeps the previous estimate and its approximate note.

notes.title: Read-only and private.
notes.text: The server copies the newest published position, runs the engine's own secondary flow on that copy with a decider that records the first question and stops, and answers only the asking seat. Nothing is persisted, logged or broadcast, the live game, its RNG and its decision log are never touched, and the worker is never waited on.

notes.title: As of now.
notes.text: The primary's own effects (Trade replenishing you, a Warfare tactical action destroying a dock), followers asked earlier in clockwise order and action cards can still change what the real question offers. The result is labelled that way, refreshed while the panel is open, and the existing validation of the plan against the real options stays authoritative.

notes.title: Which cards benefit.
notes.text: Technology (list, skips, waivers, payment plan), Construction (sites with supply and structure rules), Warfare (production builder) and, with the exact window question, Leadership (purchase facts) and the faction waivers of any card. Diplomacy gains little (exhausted planets are public), Politics, Imperial and Trade ask nothing more than follow or skip.
